title: Introduce 'safebudget' template generator and quant tagging exporter
author: Lyla Morgan
description: Context: tenant onboarding revealed repeated manual edits to prefilling templates and inconsistent quantization metadata tagging across tenants. Motivation: reduce human toil and prevent regressions in unit economics when generating tenant defaults by introducing a reproducible template generator and an exporter that attaches stable quant tags to profile artifacts. What this PR does: 1) adds a CLI service 'safebudget' that composes tenant prefill templates from workload signatures, historical token cost curves, and policy guards; 2) emits a compact quant metadata sidecar (quant-tags.json) that downstream deploy tooling and the runtime can use for safe rollouts and fallbacks; 3) integrates the generator into the existing defaults-as-code pipeline with a dry-run mode and deterministic seeding to make simulated cost calculations repeatable; 4) provides unit and integration tests, and a small set of example tenant manifests used in the quickstarts repo. Key behavior notes: templates include explicit batch/cache hints, conservative default rounding for quant profiles, and a safety min_cap parameter to avoid under-provisioning. Rollout plan: dry-run CLI in CI first, then shadow runs for 48 hours against a warmstart tenant cohort before enabling apply-on-commit. Related: references ENG-2142 and SUP-431 for incident background. Checklist: [x] CLI and library implementation; [x] unit tests for tag parsing and template composition; [x] integration smoke test in the quickstarts harness; [x] docs update in redwood-docs; [ ] follow-up: telemetry dashboard to track prefill econ impact (next PR). Links: linear:ENG-2142; jira:SUP-431.
